dependency.name: nen
dependency.minimum_semantics: MAJOR.MINOR. While nen's line is 0.x this means >=0.3.0 <0.4.0 EXACTLY -- at major zero the MINOR is the breaking-change vehicle, so a higher minor is out of range in both directions.

zero_major_caveat.$comment: An unknown key, preserved verbatim and read by nothing in nen. Its presence in this fixture is the proof of that rule.
zero_major_caveat.applies_while: the installed and pinned majors are both 0

dependency.version_probe_output: a bare semver on stdout, e.g. '0.3.0' -- no 'v' prefix, no other text
dependency.no_improvised_fallback: Unsatisfied means re-pin to pinned_ref and halt. There is no third path.

node.why: A Node install is a system-wide decision with five common answers; nen probes and reports the pin.

pnpm.why: The packageManager field states it, and corepack is the one install nen performs without reservation.

java.why: java -version writes to stderr. Two JDKs in one tree is the android lane's own problem to order.

web.why: pnpm is activated through corepack as its own step BEFORE the cached install.
nen ASSERTS the install has been run; nen never runs it, because a dependency install executes this project's own postinstall scripts.

android.why: The wrapper is the repository's own Gradle. A repo without one is a finding, not something nen installs around.

lint.why: Two commands, in order. The second alone misses the repo-wide format check.

archive.unsupported: no packaging step exists; this lane is a PWA.

deploy.unsupported: no target is wired; declare one under `targets` first.

storybook.why: An UNKNOWN verb name, preserved rather than rejected -- the ecosystem's verbs are the repository's to name.

release.unsupported: store publication is a human's, behind credentials nen never holds.

ci.$comment: Preserved verbatim; no verb reads profiles yet.
